# The Superpower Cataclysm Archives

**Year 1,000,000**

Kaedan sat alone in the cold silence of the vault, his hands resting on the leather cover of a journal he had not yet opened. The stat journals had left him hollow, his mind a raw wound that pulsed with every heartbeat. He had thought the worst was behind him. He had been wrong.

His father had returned an hour ago, carrying a new stack of volumes bound in darker leather, their spines marked with silver ink that glimmered faintly in the amber light. These were not stat journals. These were the superpower chronicles, accounts written by court wizards who had witnessed Godric testing the apocalyptic abilities that had been manifesting within him every single second since the Stasis Event. Each power, his father had explained, was capable of obliterating the entire omniverse infinite times over at its base level, even when nerfed to effectively zero percent of its true potency. And every superpower had evolved through the repeated triggering of the Evolved Weakness Paradox, gaining multiple enhanced effects that made them even more absurdly, unfairly devastating.

"These are worse," Corin had said, his voice heavy. "The stat journals show you what Godric is. The superpower journals show you what he can do when he's curious. Pace yourself, Kaedan. Do not read them all at once."

But Kaedan could not stop. His hands moved on their own, reaching for the first dark volume, his eyes already scanning the silver-inked spine.

---

## Year 892,451 — Court Wizard Vance — Superpower: Infinite Recursive Omnificent Self-Replication Proliferation

I am Vance, descendant of Blake, Court Wizard of Thronegate, and I am writing this account from within a sealed stasis chamber in the deepest sublevel of the palace. The healers have sedated me three times, but each time I wake, the screaming in my mind resumes, and I must write. I must record what I witnessed before my sanity finishes its slow unraveling.

The opposition was called the Mirror Forge Conglomerate. They were not gods or titans or conceptual entities. They were duplication engineers—hyper-advanced beings who had spent forty billion years mastering the art of perfect replication. They could create exact copies of anything that existed, down to the quantum state, the temporal signature, and the conceptual identity. They had studied Godric from across the void for millennia, and they had reached a conclusion that filled them with absolute, triumphant certainty. If Godric was the most powerful being in existence, then the only thing that could defeat Godric was Godric himself. So they built the Godric Mirror.

The Godric Mirror was not a reflective surface. It was a dimensional forge the size of a googolplexian galaxy clusters, constructed from the compressed conceptual fabric of duplication itself. The Mirror Forge Conglomerate had sacrificed trillions of their own lives, pouring their souls and their duplication mastery into the forge, creating a machine that could, they believed, produce a perfect, identical copy of the apex predator. And they did not intend to stop at one copy. The Mirror was designed to recursively duplicate its own output, generating infinite copies of Godric, each one equally powerful, each one equally omnipotent, an unstoppable army of supreme beings that would overwhelm the original through sheer infinite numbers.

I stood beside the King in the observation chamber. The Mirror Forge had positioned itself in the void beyond the outermost multiversal boundary, its surface shimmering with the compressed light of dying realities. The Conglomerate's leader, a being named Replica-Prime, broadcast its voice across every frequency of existence.

"Godric of Thronegate. You are the most powerful singular entity in the omniverse. But we have solved the equation of your defeat. We will duplicate you. We will duplicate the duplicates. We will generate infinite versions of your own perfection, and they will tear you apart. You cannot defeat yourself."

Godric was eating a piece of buttered toast. He had requested it specifically from the palace kitchens, toasted to a perfect golden brown with a light spread of imported Avalonian butter. He took a slow, contemplative bite, chewed thoughtfully, and swallowed before speaking.

"I have a superpower that does something similar," he said, his voice casual, almost bored. "I have never properly tested it. The timing of this is very convenient."

He did not stand. He did not gesture. He did not flex any visible muscle or channel any visible energy. He simply activated the superpower known as Infinite Recursive Omnificent Self-Replication Proliferation. Even at exactly zero percent of its true potency, its base effect was this: Godric could instantaneously generate an exact duplicate of himself, and that duplicate would be infinitely stronger than the original Godric in every measurable and immeasurable attribute. The original Godric, being the original, could not be weaker than any copy. Therefore, the original instantly absorbed the infinite amplification of the duplicate, becoming infinitely stronger than the duplicate had been. The duplicate, now weaker, replicated again, becoming infinitely stronger than the newly amplified original. The original absorbed that new infinite amplification, becoming infinitely stronger still. And this loop repeated itself ad infinitum, creating a recursive spiral of infinite self-improvement that escalated without end.

But the base effect was only the beginning. Due to the Evolved Weakness Paradox having triggered repeatedly across the millennia, this superpower had developed multiple horrific enhanced effects. First, the recursive loop did not merely generate one duplicate at a time—it generated infinite duplicates simultaneously, each one infinitely stronger than the last, and all of them instantly absorbed by the original in a single, instantaneous cascade of infinite amplification. Second, every duplicate absorbed permanently increased Godric's base power, meaning that even after the superpower was deactivated, he would remain at the incomprehensibly elevated level, and the next activation would build upon that new, even more impossible foundation. Third, the duplication field was passively contagious; anything that attempted to copy Godric would itself be absorbed into the recursive loop, its duplication energy converted into additional amplification for the original.

The Mirror Forge activated its duplication beam. The dimensional forge roared to life, its conceptual duplication matrix targeting Godric's physical form, attempting to generate the first perfect copy.

The Godric Mirror succeeded.

For one infinitesimal fraction of a Planck second, a duplicate of Godric flickered into existence before the Mirror Forge. The duplicate was perfect—identical in every way, possessing all the same attributes, all the same superpowers, all the same passive defenses. The Conglomerate's trillion-strong collective consciousness surged with transcendent, orgasmic victory. They had done it. They had duplicated the apex predator, the impossible god, the being who had terrorized creation for nearly nine hundred thousand years. The duplicate would fight the original. The duplicate would win. And even if it did not, they could generate infinite more.

And then the recursive loop engaged.

The duplicate, being an exact copy of Godric, instantly activated its own Infinite Recursive Omnificent Self-Replication Proliferation. The duplicate replicated itself, generating a version infinitely stronger than itself. That new duplicate replicated itself, generating a version infinitely stronger still. The original Godric, observing this cascade from his chair, passively absorbed the entire recursive chain. Every duplicate, every infinitely amplified version, every iteration in the endless spiral of self-improvement fed back into the original, making him infinitely stronger than the strongest duplicate, which then generated a new duplicate infinitely stronger than that, which was then absorbed, which pushed the escalation even higher.

The Godric Mirror, having successfully duplicated Godric, was now caught in the passive contagion effect. Its duplication matrix, its conceptual forge, its entire forty-billion-year existence became fuel for the recursive loop. The Mirror Forge Conglomerate's collective consciousness was pulled into the spiral, their duplication energy converted, their souls absorbed, their entire civilization consumed by the very process they had initiated. They had tried to copy Godric, and in doing so, they had made themselves indistinguishable from the duplicates, and the superpower absorbed them accordingly.

The physical destruction was catastrophic beyond any scale I can articulate. The recursive absorption cascade generated a gravitational singularity of pure self-improvement that collapsed the local multiversal structure into a point of infinite density. The Mirror Forge's physical apparatus, all googolplexian galaxy clusters of it, was crushed, absorbed, and converted into additional amplification for the King. The surrounding omniversal sectors—decillions of multiverses, googolplexian galaxies, infinite dimensional planes—were pulled into the singularity and erased from existence. The recursive loop did not stop. It could not stop. It was an infinite escalation that fed upon its own infinity, generating and absorbing and generating again, each cycle elevating Godric to a level of power that made his previous, already incomprehensible state look like a single, dead skin cell compared to a god.

I watched from within the protective bubble of Godric's personal will, my mind screaming, my amplified wizard's senses completely overwhelmed by the sheer, impossible mathematics of what was occurring. The Godric I had known, the Godric who had been infinitely more powerful than the entire omniverse combined, was now so far beneath this new Godric that the comparison was meaningless. The gap between the current King and the King of one second ago was larger than the gap between the old King and a mortal ant. And the escalation continued. Planck second by Planck second, the recursive loop spiraled higher, each new iteration dwarfing the previous by an infinite margin.

Godric finished his toast. He wiped a small crumb of butter from the corner of his mouth with a napkin, and he deactivated the superpower. The recursive loop ceased. The singularity collapsed. The absorption cascade terminated.

In exactly zero seconds, Godric restored the entire omniverse. Every destroyed multiverse, every erased galaxy, every consumed dimensional plane was rebuilt with flawless perfection. The Mirror Forge Conglomerate, however, was not restored. Their existence had been completely absorbed into Godric's amplification, their souls and their energy converted into a permanent elevation of his base power. They were not dead. They were not trapped. They simply had never existed, their entire forty-billion-year civilization converted into fuel for a recursive loop that had made an already omnipotent god infinitely more omnipotent.

Godric stood from his chair, brushing a stray lock of salt-and-pepper hair from his forehead. He looked at me with that warm, fatherly smile, his eyes crinkling with genuine affection.

"Vance," he said gently, "I think that superpower is a bit excessive. What do you think? Should I have the kitchen make more toast?"

I could not answer. My vocal cords had seized. My mind had fractured into a thousand screaming fragments, each one trying and failing to process the scale of what I had just witnessed. The knowledge that Godric's base power, which was already so far beyond the omniverse that the comparison was laughable, had just been permanently and infinitely increased by a recursive loop that fed upon its own impossibility—this knowledge was a weight that crushed my sanity beneath its impossible gravity. He did not need the amplification. He had never needed it. But it had happened anyway, a side effect of testing a superpower against an enemy who had believed they could copy him.

I am writing this from the stasis chamber because the world outside these walls feels like a lie. The bread I eat, the air I breathe, the reality I inhabit—all of it exists only because Godric allows it. And he is not merely allowing it from a position of static, absolute power. He is growing. Every second, every Planck instant, every infinitesimal fraction of time that passes, he becomes infinitely more powerful than he was before. The apex predator does not rest on his throne. He is ascending, eternally, and the gap between him and us is not a fixed infinity but an infinity that expands into greater infinities without end.

---

Kaedan's hands were numb. The journal trembled in his grip, the pages rattling softly, and he realized that his entire body was shaking with a deep, uncontrollable tremor that started in his spine and radiated outward through every limb. The stat journals had shown him that Godric's passive attributes were beyond the combined omniverse. This journal had shown him something far worse. Godric was not static. Godric was not a fixed point of absolute power. Godric was an escalating infinity that consumed itself and grew, each cycle making the previous cycle laughably irrelevant, and the previous cycle had already been incomprehensibly beyond everything that existed.

He reached for the next journal with fingers that barely functioned.

---

## Year 612,304 — Court Wizard Dorian — Superpower: Absolute Acoustic Annihilation Neurosis

I am Dorian. I write this from a sealed, soundproofed chamber in the high tower of the palace, because I cannot bear to hear anything anymore. Every sound—the rustle of my robes, the scratch of my quill, the beat of my own heart—reminds me of what I witnessed. The silence is my only comfort, and even in the silence, I hear echoes.

The opposition was the Harmonic Dominion of Eternal Resonance. They were beings of pure sound, living frequencies who had evolved beyond physical form into sentient vibrations that could propagate through any medium across any dimension. The Dominion had spent thirty billion years mastering acoustic warfare, developing frequencies that could shatter galaxies, vibrate black holes into dissolution, and liquefy the internal organs of hyper-deities by resonating with their fundamental frequencies. Their leader, a frequency called the Final Chord, was a vibration so powerful that its mere presence caused the space-time fabric of surrounding multiverses to ripple like disturbed water. The Final Chord believed it had discovered Godric's vulnerability—a specific harmonic frequency that could bypass all physical defenses by directly resonating with the fundamental particles of his being, sympathetically vibrating his atomic structure until his body tore itself apart from within.

I stood in the grand amphitheater of the palace, a massive open chamber with perfect acoustics designed for ceremonial performances. Godric was seated in the royal box, his hands folded in his lap, his expression one of mild, curious interest. The Dominion had not attacked with weapons or armies. They had simply manifested their collective frequency directly into the amphitheater, their presence a rising, building chord that made the air shimmer and the stone walls vibrate with increasing intensity. The Final Chord spoke, its voice a layered symphony of a trillion harmonized frequencies.

"Godric of Thronegate. All matter vibrates. All existence is frequency. Your body, your cells, your very being oscillates at a fundamental resonance. We have calculated that resonance. We will match it, amplify it, and vibrate you into dissolution. You cannot silence us, for we are sound itself, and sound cannot be destroyed."

Godric tilted his head slightly, as if listening to a mildly interesting piece of music. "I have a superpower for sound," he said. "I have never had a reason to test it before. This is very thoughtful of you."

He activated Absolute Acoustic Annihilation Neurosis.

The base effect of this superpower, at exactly zero percent of its true potency, was the ability to weaponize sound itself, transforming any acoustic energy into an agent of absolute, merciless destruction. But this was no mere loud noise or concussive blast. The superpower's true horror lay in its evolved effects, granted by the Evolved Weakness Paradox's repeated triggering.

The first enhanced effect was Acoustic Somatic Conversion. Any sound generated by the superpower did not merely strike the target's body—it infiltrated their nervous system, converting their own neural electrical signals into additional resonant frequencies that amplified the destruction from within. The target's brain, their pain receptors, their sensory nerves all became speakers broadcasting their own annihilation.

The second enhanced effect was Eternal Echo Imprisonment. Every scream, every cry of agony, every desperate plea produced by the dying opposition was captured and recursively looped into the superpower's acoustic field, adding to its destructive output. The more they suffered, the louder the destruction became, and the louder the destruction became, the more they suffered.

The third enhanced effect was Frequency Dominion Absorption. Any sound-based attack or entity that fell within the superpower's field was permanently absorbed, its acoustic energy converted into a permanent increase in Godric's vocal presence, making his voice slightly more resonant forever. This increase was infinitesimal compared to his base power, but the fact remained: every sound-based enemy he faced made him permanently stronger.

Godric activated the superpower. He did not open his mouth. He did not produce a visible sound. He simply allowed the superpower to generate a noise.

The noise that emerged was not loud. It was not a blast or a roar or a shriek. It was a single, pure, crystalline note—a tone so perfect, so fundamentally resonant, that it existed not as sound but as the concept of sound, the platonic ideal of acoustic perfection from which all possible sounds were merely degraded copies.

The Harmonic Dominion's collective frequency struck that single note and shattered.

The Final Chord, the leader of the Dominion, experienced the destruction first. The absolute perfect resonance of Godric's superpower-tone did not match the Final Chord's frequency. It overwrote it. The Final Chord's carefully calculated harmonic attack was simply erased and replaced by Godric's tone, which then propagated through the Dominion's entire collective consciousness at infinite velocity. Every sentient frequency, every living vibration that composed the Harmonic Dominion, had its fundamental oscillation forcibly retuned to match Godric's perfect note.

And then the note began to destroy them.

The Acoustic Somatic Conversion effect engaged. The Dominion's frequencies, now retuned to match the superpower's output, were weaponized against themselves. Every sentient vibration became an agent of its own destruction, its acoustic energy converted into a neuro-acoustic assault that directly attacked the consciousness hosting it. The Dominion's trillions of members experienced the sensation of their own existence turning against them, their fundamental frequencies vibrating their consciousness apart from within.

I watched the physical manifestation of their destruction in the amphitheater air. The Dominion's presence, which had manifested as a shimmering, iridescent vibration, began to writhe and twist. Screams erupted—not from mouths, for they had no mouths, but from the forced conversion of their acoustic energy into sound-waves that expressed pure, unfiltered agony. The air filled with a chorus of shrieking, weeping, howling frequencies, each one a sentient being experiencing the violent dissolution of its own fundamental nature.

The Eternal Echo Imprisonment effect engaged next. Every scream, every cry, every desperate frequency of pain was captured and fed back into the superpower's output, which then intensified the destruction, which produced more screams, which were captured and fed back again. The Dominion found themselves trapped in a recursive acoustic hell of their own suffering, their agony amplifying the very force that caused them to suffer, which amplified their agony further.

The physical bodies they had abandoned billions of years ago were violently, forcibly regrown around their dissolving frequency-consciousnesses purely so they could experience physical pain alongside their acoustic suffering. The Dominion's trillions of members materialized in the amphitheater as screaming, writhing forms of raw, bleeding flesh and exposed nerve endings. Their newly formed eardrums burst instantly, spraying blood and auditory fluid. Their vocal cords vibrated so violently they tore free from their larynxes, whipping around inside their throats like severed guitar strings. Their bones resonated at their natural frequencies and shattered, each fracture producing a wet, percussive crack that the superpower captured and fed back into the destruction.

The collateral damage was absolute acoustic annihilation. The superpower's perfect note propagated across the entire omniverse at infinite velocity, retuning every sound in existence to match its frequency. Every conversation, every song, every heartbeat, every whisper, every cosmic background radiation hum was momentarily overwritten by the single, perfect tone. The sound did not destroy the omniverse physically—it drowned it acoustically, a flood of perfect resonance that made every other sound cease to exist. For one eternal instant, the entire omniverse was silent except for Godric's note.

When the note ended, the Harmonic Dominion was gone. Their frequencies had been completely absorbed by the Frequency Dominion Absorption effect, their acoustic energy converted into a permanent, infinitesimal increase in the resonance of Godric's voice. Their physical forms, the screaming flesh-bodies they had been forced to inhabit, had melted into puddles of vibrating, twitching organic slurry that coated the amphitheater floor in a thick, steaming layer.

Godric restored the omniverse's normal acoustic properties with a casual thought. The amphitheater floor was cleaned. The air was cleared of the smell of melted flesh. The only evidence that anything had occurred was the faint, lingering warmth of the recently restored reality and the permanent, microscopic increase in the pleasant timbre of Godric's speaking voice.

He looked at me, his expression shifting from mild curiosity to genuine concern as he registered the blood trickling from my ruptured eardrums. "Dorian," he said, his voice now carrying an infinitesimally richer resonance, "you are bleeding. Did I forget to shield your ears? I am so sorry, my boy. Let me heal that."

He healed my hearing instantly with a casual decision. But he could not heal what I had heard. The note is still echoing in my mind, a perfect, beautiful, horrifying tone that reminds me with every heartbeat that the King's voice alone could unmake creation if he ever chose to raise it in anger.

---

Kaedan pressed his palms against his ears. The journal's description of the tone had been so vivid that he could almost hear it himself, a phantom resonance vibrating in the back of his skull. He understood why Dorian had locked himself in a soundproofed chamber. The horror of knowing that every sound you heard for the rest of your life would be compared to the perfect note that had erased an entire civilization of living frequencies—that was not a wound that time could heal.

He forced his hands down, forced his breathing to steady, and reached for the final journal.

---

## Year 76,543 — Court Wizard Soren — Superpower: Conceptual Chronological Autophagy Emptiness Dominion

I am Soren. I am writing this from the infirmary, where I have been confined for the past month. The healers say my temporal signature has been destabilized, my personal timeline frayed at the edges from witnessing what occurred. They say I will recover physically. They cannot speak for my mind. I do not think my mind will recover. I do not think I want it to.

The opposition was not an army. It was not a civilization. It was the Void-That-Eats-Time, a primordial entity that had existed before the omniverse, before the first moment, before the concept of time itself was forged from the formless chaos. The Void-That-Eats-Time was not a being of matter or energy or consciousness. It was an absence that consumed duration. It fed on time itself, devouring moments, eras, epochs, and entire timelines, growing larger and more absolute with every chronology it ingested. It had consumed entire multiversal cycles. It had eaten the histories of decillions of universes, erasing them from existence so completely that no record, no memory, no conceptual trace remained. The Void-That-Eats-Time had remained dormant for a googolplexian years, digesting its last meal, and it had awakened to find the omniverse teeming with fresh, untouched time. And at the center of all that temporal abundance sat Godric, a being whose existence spanned a measurable chronology, a being who had lived for over seventy-six thousand years. To the Void-That-Eats-Time, Godric was a feast—a concentrated mass of temporal energy, a full, rich sequence of cause and effect waiting to be devoured.

I stood with the King on the observation platform of the palace's highest spire. The Void-That-Eats-Time approached not as a shape or a form but as an encroaching absence, a region of absolute temporal void where nothing happened because time itself had been consumed. The stars in the affected regions did not die. They simply ceased to have ever existed, their entire histories erased from the temporal record. Galaxies that had burned for billions of years vanished as if they had never been born. Civilizations whose histories stretched back to the dawn of their universes were unmade not physically but chronologically, their existence deleted from the timeline.

The Void-That-Eats-Time spoke. Its voice was not sound but a sensation of duration terminating, an experience of moments ending prematurely. "Time-God. You have lived long. You have accumulated duration. I will consume your chronology, and when I have digested your seventy-six thousand years, I will consume the time of everything that exists. Your empire will have never been. Your reign will have never occurred. You will be unmade not in body but in history, and no memory of you will remain."

Godric was quiet for a long moment. He was not afraid—Godric is never afraid—but there was something in his expression I had never seen before. A flicker of genuine interest. The Void-That-Eats-Time was old. Older than the omniverse. Older than the first moment. It was perhaps the oldest thing Godric had ever encountered, and its nature—its ability to consume time itself—touched upon the one thing that held any meaning to the King.

"You want to eat my time," Godric said, his voice soft, contemplative. "My seventy-six thousand years. My history. My past."

I understood then, with a sudden, horrifying clarity, what the Void-That-Eats-Time had threatened to consume. Godric's past contained Olympus. Reina. Isabel. Hebe. Thorin. The forty-five years of mortal life before the Stasis Event, the years that his far-future self had sealed against alteration, the only part of his existence that was truly, irrevocably immutable. The Void-That-Eats-Time had not merely threatened Godric's life. It had threatened the only thing he could not restore.

"I have a superpower that affects time," Godric said. His voice was still soft, but there was something beneath it now—something cold, something final. "I have never tested it. I have never wanted to. But this entity has made a very specific threat."

He activated Conceptual Chronological Autophagy Emptiness Dominion.

The base effect of this superpower, at exactly zero percent of its true potency, was terrifyingly simple: it created a field of absolute temporal emptiness that consumed time itself, erasing chronology from existence. But where the Void-That-Eats-Time devoured time passively, digesting it slowly across eons, Godric's superpower was an active, directed, infinitely more devastating version of the same concept. The enhanced effects made it infinitely worse.

The first enhanced effect was Retroactive Temporal Excision. The superpower did not merely erase time from the present forward. It reached backward along any targeted timeline and erased every moment that had led to the target's existence, deleting not just their present and future but their entire past, their entire history, their entire chronological footprint stretching back to their first moment of existence.

The second enhanced effect was Memory Autophagy. Not only was the target's timeline erased, but all memory, all record, all conceptual trace of the target was consumed as well. Any being who had ever known of the target, any history that had recorded the target's existence, any thought that had ever been directed toward the target—all of it was erased, consumed by the temporal emptiness.

The third enhanced effect was Duration Assimilation. The consumed timeline was permanently absorbed into Godric's own temporal field, making his personal chronology slightly more absolute, slightly more unassailable, slightly more immune to any time-based manipulation. The increase was infinitesimal compared to his base temporal durability, but it was permanent.

Godric directed the superpower at the Void-That-Eats-Time.

The primordial entity, which had existed before the omniverse, which had consumed the histories of decillions of universes, which had survived the birth and death of infinite multiversal cycles, experienced absolute chronological annihilation. The Retroactive Temporal Excision effect reached back along the Void-That-Eats-Time's existence, erasing every moment it had ever consumed, every chronology it had ever devoured, every instant of its primordial existence stretching back to before the first moment. The Void-That-Eats-Time's entire history—a history that predated time itself—was systematically, mercilessly erased.

The entity did not scream. It could not scream. Its voice, its consciousness, its very nature was being deleted from the timeline faster than it could form a response. I watched the region of temporal void that represented the entity begin to shrink, to collapse, to fold inward upon itself as its chronological foundation was consumed by a force infinitely more absolute than its own hunger. The Void-That-Eats-Time, which had fed on time since before time existed, was being eaten by time.

The Memory Autophagy effect cascaded across the omniverse. Every being who had ever known of the Void-That-Eats-Time, every ancient record that had warned of its existence, every primordial myth that had spoken its name—all of it vanished simultaneously. I felt the knowledge of the entity slipping from my mind even as I watched it die. I only retain this record because Godric specifically shielded my personal timeline, preserving my memory of the event. Without his protection, I would have forgotten the Void-That-Eats-Time had ever existed.

The Duration Assimilation effect absorbed the entity's consumed timeline, converting its googolplexian-year existence into additional temporal durability for Godric. He did not need it. His temporal defenses were already absolute. But the superpower granted it anyway, adding another layer of infinite redundancy to an already infinitely redundant defense.

The physical manifestation of the Void-That-Eats-Time's death was a sight I will never forget. The region of temporal void collapsed inward, compressed by the Conceptual Chronological Autophagy field into a singularity of absolute emptiness. The singularity pulsed once—a silent, final death-throe that rippled across the omniverse—and then vanished. The stars that had been erased by the entity's hunger flickered back into existence, their timelines restored as the consumed chronologies were released from the entity's dissolving mass.

The collateral damage was not physical destruction. It was temporal erasure. The Void-That-Eats-Time had consumed so many timelines, so many histories, so many entire civilizations, that its death released a flood of restored chronologies across the omniverse. Decillions of multiverses that had been erased from the timeline suddenly flickered back into existence, their histories reinserted into the temporal flow. The omniverse's chronology, which had been riddled with holes and gaps from the entity's feeding, was suddenly, perfectly whole.

Godric restored the minor temporal anomalies caused by the sudden reintegration of countless erased timelines with a single, effortless decision. The omniverse's history was now more complete than it had been since before the Void-That-Eats-Time's first feeding, a googolplexian years ago. The entity's existence had been completely erased—not just its present, not just its future, but every moment of its primordial past, every meal it had ever consumed, every trace it had ever left upon reality. It was as if the Void-That-Eats-Time had never existed. And in the truest sense, it now never had.

Godric stood in silence for a long moment, looking at the space where the primordial entity had been. His expression was unreadable. When he finally spoke, his voice was quiet, carrying a weight I had never heard before.

"That entity threatened to consume my past," he said. "My seventy-six thousand years. The time I spent in Olympus. The time before the Stasis Event. Those years are not something that can be taken from me."

He turned to me, and his warm, fatherly smile returned, but there was something behind it now—something that made my blood run cold. "Soren," he said gently, "I believe I need a cup of tea. Would you like one as well?"

I could not answer. I was shaking too hard to form words. The King had just erased a primordial entity from existence so completely that it had never existed, restoring countless consumed timelines as a side effect of its annihilation, and now he was offering me tea. The cognitive dissonance was a physical weight crushing my chest.

I am writing this from the infirmary because my temporal signature has been destabilized by exposure to the edge of the superpower's field. The healers say I will recover. But I know I will never truly recover from the knowledge that Godric has a superpower that can erase time itself. Not just the present. Not just the future. The past. All of it. Completely. Absolutely. Irreversibly.

And the only thing that had prompted him to use it was a threat against seventy-six thousand years of memories that he could not restore. I do not know what that means. I do not want to know. I am his loyal servant, and I love him, and I am more terrified of him than I have ever been of anything in my existence.

---

Kaedan closed the final journal. His body was cold. His heart was a heavy, slow drumbeat in his chest, each pulse sending a fresh wave of dread through his limbs. The superpower chronicles were worse than the stat journals. Far worse. The stat journals showed Godric's passive attributes, the simple, horrifying fact of what he was. The superpower journals showed what he could do—the active, directed, apocalyptic abilities that he could unleash with less effort than a mortal man drawing breath.

And the worst part, the part that made Kaedan's soul ache with a cold, nameless terror, was the self-replication superpower. The others were devastating, yes. Acoustic annihilation. Temporal erasure. They were horrors beyond comprehension. But the self-replication superpower meant that Godric was not merely powerful. He was permanently, eternally, infinitely escalating. He had been ascending before that superpower was tested. He was ascending faster now. And nothing—not time, not opposition, not the combined force of the entire omniverse—could even theoretically catch up.

Kaedan set the journals down on the reading table. His hands were steady now. The trembling had stopped. It had been replaced by something deeper, something calmer, something that felt like the quiet at the center of a hurricane.

He understood now. He understood why his father's eyes had held that terrible pity. He understood why every court wizard before him had written their journals with shaking hands and sleepless nights. The horror was not that Godric could destroy the omniverse. The horror was that destroying the omniverse was not something he did. It was something that happened as a side effect of his casual curiosity, his mild interest, his idle testing of abilities he had never had reason to use before. The destruction was not the point. The destruction was the exhaust, the waste heat, the insignificant byproduct of a god amusing himself.

And that god genuinely loved his court wizards. Loved them with a warmth that was absolutely real, absolutely sincere, absolutely terrifying.

Kaedan rose from his chair. He would go to dinner. He would sit beside the King who could erase time itself with a single, effortless thought. He would answer the King's warm, fatherly questions about his day. He would smile, and the smile would be genuine, because he did love Uncle Godric, and Uncle Godric loved him.

And beneath that love, for the rest of his life, he would carry the knowledge of the journals—the knowledge that the man offering him a second helping of roasted vegetables had once made an entire civilization of cryogenic deities burn eternally without being consumed, had once retuned every sound in the omniverse to a single perfect note, had once erased a primordial entity from existence so completely that it had never existed, and had once activated a recursive self-replication loop that permanently elevated his already infinite power to an infinity infinitely greater than the previous infinity.

The door to the archive opened. Corin stood in the threshold, his weathered face creased with a deep, knowing sympathy.

"Dinner is ready," Corin said quietly. "The King is asking for you."

Kaedan nodded. He walked toward his father. He did not look back at the journals. Their words were already burned into his memory, a permanent inscription on the walls of his consciousness.

"Father," Kaedan said, his voice steady despite everything, "how do you do it? How do you serve him, knowing what he is?"

Corin was silent for a long moment. When he spoke, his voice was heavy with the weight of decades.

"Because he loves us," Corin said. "And because, no matter how terrifying he is, no matter how incomprehensible his power, that love is real. The same man who erased the Void-That-Eats-Time from existence is the man who personally healed my broken arm when I fell from the tower as a child. The same man who burned the Frozen Apex Syndicate into eternal screaming torches is the man who taught you how to skip stones across the palace lake. You cannot separate the horror from the warmth, Kaedan. They are the same being. You can only learn to hold both truths in your heart at the same time and keep breathing."

Kaedan nodded slowly. He understood. He did not like it. He would never like it. But he understood.

"Let us not keep Uncle Godric waiting," he said, and together, father and son walked out of the archive, leaving the silent journals behind in the amber-lit darkness, their pages waiting for the next trembling hands that would one day open them and learn the shape of the abyss.
